Check the quality of the calibrated probabilities by species

Source: R/calibration_quality.R
calibration_quality.Rd

compare_calibration_models() scores each model over all the clips, which can hide a species whose probabilities should not be trusted: the mean AUC rises when species differ in precision, even if the score says little within a species, and partial pooling lends such a species the curve of the others. This function refits one model by cross-validation and scores the held-out predictions within each group, asking three questions before the probabilities are used:

Usage

calibration_quality(
  validations,
  formula,
  k_folds = 5,
  seed = 2026,
  fold_group = NULL,
  by = "species",
  min_class = 10,
  auc_min = 0.7,
  slope_range = c(0.5, 1.5),
  intercept_max = 1
)

Arguments

validations

Table returned by read_validations().

formula

Formula of the model to check, e.g. the one chosen by select_calibration_model().

k_folds

Number of folds.

seed

Seed of the fold assignment. The global random number generator is left as it was.

fold_group

Optional character vector of grouping columns. Do not include species, verdicts or confidence scores: these would split recordings or nights by species or by outcome. Group IDs must be nonmissing and nonempty. NULL keeps the original clip folds.

by

Columns that define the groups: "species", or c("site", "species") for the cells of the calibration, which hold fewer clips each.

min_class

Least number of true positives and of false positives for a group to be judged. With fewer, status is "insufficient".

auc_min

Lowest acceptable auc and auc_score.

slope_range

Acceptable range of cal_slope.

intercept_max

Largest acceptable absolute cal_intercept.

Value

A tibble with one row per group: the by columns, n, n_tp, n_fp, conf_min, conf_max, auc, auc_score, logloss, logloss_null, logloss_gain, cal_intercept, cal_slope, status ("ok", "poor" or "insufficient") and reason. Measures that cannot be computed (e.g. the AUC of a group with one verdict) are NA. Folds whose fit failed are left out, with a warning.

Details

  • Does the model add information? logloss_gain is the log-loss of a null model, the share of true positives of the group in the training folds, minus the log-loss of the model. It plays the part of a comparison with an intercept-only model, on held-out clips.

  • Does it discriminate? auc is the AUC of the held-out probabilities within the group, and auc_score that of the raw confidence score. An auc well above auc_score means that the discrimination comes from other terms of the model (e.g. site effects, when by = "species"), not from the score, so both must reach auc_min. Unlike the AUC of compare_calibration_models(), these are not reversed when the ranking is inverted, so values below 0.5 can occur.

  • Are the probabilities correct? cal_intercept and cal_slope come from a logistic regression of the verdicts on the logit of the held-out probabilities (intercept 0 and slope 1 when well calibrated). AUC alone does not answer this: a model can rank clips well and still give wrong probabilities.

The default limits behind status (auc_min, slope_range, intercept_max and min_class) are provisional screening values. They were chosen by judgement, and were neither derived from the literature nor validated on data, so a group near a limit is not a clear pass or fail. They are meant to direct attention to a group, and should be reviewed and set for each project. Read the measures along with status. A group marked "poor" needs more clips, a different model or a decision to leave the species out of the analyses that use P(TP).

The results depend on the design of the review. Discrimination is measured over the scores that were reviewed, so the "top" design, which concentrates the clips at high scores (see conf_min and conf_max), can give a low AUC even with a good classifier. The clips of "random_detections" cover the range of scores of the predictions.

The fits use maximum likelihood, also when the final model is fitted with engine = "brms". Use fold_group to keep the clips of a recording or night on the same side of the split.

See also

compare_calibration_models(), calibration_ppc()
